name: Beelzebub
description: Category A: name origin 2 Kings 1:2-3,6,16 ("Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron" -- Philistine deity consulted by King Ahaziah; the name likely means 'lord of the flies,' possibly a mocking corruption of 'Baal-zebul,' lord of the [heavenly] dwelling). By the Gospels the name has migrated to mean chief of demons (Matthew 12:24). Milton's elaborate characterization as Satan's chief lieutenant and orator in the infernal council (Book II) is Miltonic invention (D) built on a one-line biblical name. See docs/milton/character-catalog.md §II.
narrative_function: Satan's closest ally, first roused from the burning lake, presents Satan's plan to the infernal council.
